rows.evidence: Sections 1–2 impose prospective constraints on agency expenditure for earmarks in later legislation, including statutory or merit-based decisions. Section 2(b) conditions use of congressional views on writing and normally requires posting written recommendations within 30 days. Sections 2(c) and (d) provide original OMB implementation and reporting-on-request responsibilities. This is a prospective recurrent rule rather than an action exhausted by issuing it. An implementing memo can establish conduct in its own time.
rows.status: 2026 continuing operation remains indeterminate on supplied original and bounded research. A contemporaneous implementation finding cannot prove cutoff applicability, and omission of a later instrument in indexes cannot prove survival.
rows.lifecycle: Open; no established first-ending date or complete chain.

rows.evidence: Original issued 2006-02-07. Section 9 operative at 12:01 a.m. EST Feb 8, not the Feb 10 publication date. Creates emergency, asset blocking and transactions prohibitions with exceptions and a Treasury designation/reporting regime. EO 13739 expressly revokes the order and terminates emergency. Section 3 fixes 8:00 a.m. EDT Sept 14, 2016. Section 1 preserves actions taken and pending undecided proceedings, earlier-act proceedings and rights/duties matured and penalties incurred. This proves the event and its legal savings, not absence of surviving consequences.
rows.status: Prospective authority ended at that event. Cutoff revival/other later authority, individual activity and all claims require bounded supplemental examination. No whole-order status adoption.
rows.lifecycle: Open; express cessation is a bounded fact, not a complete chain establishing earliest ending of every clause/individual application.

rows.evidence: 1994 order adopted minimum seismic standards, allowed qualifying existing evaluations, directed inventory and estimates at four years, initial and biennial reporting and periodic standard updates. EO 13717 section 5 expressly revokes 12941 and 12699; dated Feb 2, 2016, issued with present-tense revocation, published Feb 5. No separate effective hour in text; neither later guidance deadlines nor publication automatically sets time of revocation. Similar replacement duties derive from the new instrument. Completed assessments/records and effects on buildings remain distinct from command survival.
rows.status: The express 2016 event establishes loss of prospective authority then, with cutoff revival/intervening legal history left open. No inferred retroactive unmaking of past acts.
rows.lifecycle: Open; earliest endings at provision level, amendment/implementation history, competing evidence and independent gates unadjudicated.
